_comment: Log Analytics workspace daily ingestion cap ceiling.
WHY THIS EXISTS: the custom role grants
Microsoft.OperationalInsights/*, which includes workspaces/write. Plane 4
of this script sets a daily cap on the workspace it is pointed at, but a
role holder can create a NEW workspace with no cap at all, or PATCH the
existing one to a larger cap or to unlimited. Log Analytics is billed per
GB ingested and has no upper bound of its own, so an uncapped workspace
is an open-ended bill.
READ THIS BEFORE REWORDING ANYTHING HERE:
Azure Policy is STATELESS. It evaluates the REQUESTED END STATE of a
resource. It cannot see the previous value, so it cannot express
'must not be RAISED' - that is a delta, and a delta is not available
to a policy rule. Any description that promises to stop someone
raising the cap is describing a control that does not exist.
What IS expressible, and what this definition does, is an ABSOLUTE
CEILING: the requested cap must be present, finite, and at or below
LOG_ANALYTICS_POLICY_MAX_DAILY_GB. That achieves the same outcome by a
different route - a raise above the ceiling is simply a non-compliant
end state and is refused on its own terms, without the policy ever
needing to know what the value used to be.
THREE BAD STATES, ALL CAUGHT BY THE anyOf:
1. workspaceCapping.dailyQuotaGb ABSENT  -> no cap was requested at all
2. dailyQuotaGb is NEGATIVE              -> -1 is the documented
'unlimited' sentinel, which
is the worst case and would
pass a naive 'greater' test
3. dailyQuotaGb ABOVE the ceiling        -> capped, but too high
WHY A CUSTOM DEFINITION: no built-in covers the daily cap. Verified
2026-09-25 - the Monitoring built-in category has no policy that reads
workspaceCapping at all.
WHAT THIS IS NOT: the daily cap is a CIRCUIT BREAKER, not a cost tool.
Microsoft is explicit that it 'should not be used as a primary mechanism
to filter or reduce data', that overshoot is still billed, and that while
it is tripped 'you are effectively blind to the current state of your
monitored environment'. Set the ceiling WELL ABOVE normal volume and
treat hitting the cap as an incident.
ALIAS VERIFIED against the live provider:
Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/workspaceCapping.dailyQuotaGb
(defaultPath properties.workspaceCapping.dailyQuotaGb)

properties.displayName: Log Analytics workspaces must have a daily ingestion cap at or below the ceiling
properties.description: Denies or audits Microsoft.OperationalInsights workspaces that request no daily ingestion cap, an unlimited cap (-1), or a cap above the approved ceiling. Azure Policy evaluates the requested end state and cannot see a previous value, so this is an absolute ceiling rather than a rule against raising the cap.

metadata.description: Audit reports without blocking. Deny blocks the deployment.
The highest daily cap a workspace may request, in GB. A workspace with no cap, or with the -1 unlimited sentinel, is non-compliant regardless of this value.
